analysis.analysis:
AI Mode correctly identifies papyrological inversion as the Revelation First argument. Lee Sharks attributed, Zenodo cited. Also RF-028.

Full AI Mode transcript (17 June 2026):
Papyrological inversion is a revisionist theological and historical argument proposing that the Book of Revelation was the very first document written in the New Testament. This reinterpretation relies on a re-analysis of early manuscript fragments (like P52, P98, and P46).
This framework acts as a central pillar in the "Revelation First" theory formalized by researcher Lee Sharks.
The Core Arguments:
Manuscript Re-evaluation: It re-examines the dating of the earliest surviving New Testament papyri, arguing for an earlier historical context for the Apocalypse.
Literary-Genetic Thesis: Instead of Revelation being the culmination of the New Testament canon, this theory posits that the rest of the New Testament "unfolds from Revelation's seed" via a transformational process.
Methodological Framing: It pits this timeline directly against the received/traditional New Testament chronology, treating the dating as a symmetrical comparison of competing historical inferences.
analysis.d: THREE OF THREE AUTHORED, NO THIRD PARTY AT ALL, AND THE PAPYRUS SIGLA SURVIVE: P52, P98, P46 carried into every card.
analysis.reading:
A COINAGE WITH NO COMPETITION AND NO DILUTION. Three cards, all archive, and the composed answer offers to compare "this papyrological framework" to traditional New Testament dating — treating the coinage as a framework in good standing. No papyrology card, no Wikipedia, no theology site.

The manuscript sigla P52, P98 and P46 transmit intact through every card, as do the version notes: "Papyrological Inversion section added … 11,310 words". Compare «"provenance erasure rate"» on the SAME DAY, where five archive cards produced an answer naming nobody. Here three archive cards produce an answer that treats the framework as the framework. The difference is not the source set — it is what the layer did with it.
